name: payment-frame
description:
A third-party checkout, embedded. It is a unit for the reason that makes it awkward: the iframe's inside belongs to somebody else and cannot be styled, so the only thing this system controls is the FRAME around it — the height it reserves, what shows while it loads, and what shows when it does not. Those three are exactly what a payment surface gets wrong, and getting them wrong looks like a broken page at the moment someone is about to pay.

On my.aven.ceo this was 246 lines with the state machine and the layout mixed together, and the states — loading, ready, expired, failed — spelled as bare `.checkout-state` text.

base.$description: CONTAINER. This unit establishes an inline-size container named after itself, so anything inside it can respond to the width of THIS BOX rather than to the width of the window. That is the difference that matters for a design system: a composite dropped into a 320px sidebar and the same composite on a 320px phone are the same situation, and a viewport query calls them different ones. The library carries no viewport media query anywhere for exactly this reason — the only `@media` in it is `prefers-reduced-motion`, which is a person's setting and not a size.

stage.$description: A RESERVED box, not a box that grows. `min-block-size` before the iframe loads is the whole point: a payment form that appears and shoves the page down is a layout shift at the exact moment someone is reading an amount, and it is the one CLS failure that costs money. The provider decides what is inside; we decide that the space is already there.

state.$description: What is happening, in words. It was a bare `.checkout-state` with the text carrying everything; `role=status` is what makes it reach a screen reader when it changes, which is the only way a non-sighted user learns the form failed.

fallback.$description: The link out, for when the embed does not load — a blocked third-party frame, a strict extension, a browser that refuses it. A payment surface with no route out when its iframe fails is a dead end on the one page that must not have one.

status.$description: Where the payment is. It dresses the STATE line, not the stage — a frame that turns red says the page failed when what failed is one attempt.

a11y.note: `aria-busy` on the section while the frame loads, and `role=status` on the state line so a change is announced without interrupting. The iframe itself needs a `title` — an untitled iframe is announced as 'frame' and nothing else, which on a payment page is the least acceptable place for it. Focus must not be trapped: the fallback link has to remain reachable by keyboard even while the embed is present, because a frame that eats Tab is a frame nobody can leave.
